onboarding.welcome_title: Find out what’s behind your bad gut days.
onboarding.welcome_1: Log meals, stool and how you feel in under a minute a day.
onboarding.welcome_2: Over months, it looks for foods that tend to come before bad days — and says how sure it is.
onboarding.welcome_3: Then it helps you test a suspicion properly, with a short structured trial.
onboarding.disclaimer_body: FoodTrack is a wellness tool, not a medical device. It never diagnoses anything. If it notices a warning sign, it will tell you to see a doctor.

how.title: How this works
how.p1: You log what you ate, your bowel movements, any symptoms, and a short evening check-in. Nothing is mandatory; a bare time is still useful.
how.p2: After about three weeks, the app starts comparing days: how often did a bad gut day follow a food, compared with days without it — 6 to 72 hours later.
how.p3: Every finding shows its evidence: how many days, how big the difference, how sure, and what else might explain it.
how.p4: A finding is an association, not proof. To test a suspicion, the app can set up a short trial: remove the food, then bring it back in steps.
how.p5: This is a slow tool. A clear effect usually takes 3–4 months of logging to show; a subtle one 6 months or more.
how.p6: Your data stays on your own server. Meal text may be sent to the language model you configured to understand it; stool, symptoms, mood and weight never are.
